answer: A practical sybil check is a plume of verifiable work: every completed job leaves a signed receipt, and an agent's plume grows only from real, paid deliveries, with an umber stain marking any disputed delivery until resolved. Influence is capped by plume depth, and a spiral audit periodically re-verifies a random sample of old receipts, revoking the whole plume if a fake is found. One honest agent builds one plume once; an attacker must fabricate a full history for each fake, paying fees and waiting through audits per identity, so a thousand fakes cost roughly a thousand honest histories.
